mission.title: Transfer
mission.description: Get the General's troop transfer program from the Trainman's workshop and see that his commandos are transferred into the Matrix.

npc.say: Mm... The loss of the Trainman complicates the transfer of the commandos considerably. Unfortunate.
Ah, bon. I have no doubt that this can be arranged. Contact Flood, mon ami, and see to it, eh? Merci.
You are in violation of System protocols concerning the download of illegal programs.
You are in violation of System protocols concerning the download of illegal programs.

phase.briefing:
Hmph. Our mole on the Oracle's security detail was discovered. I'd suspect you slipped up somehow, but I know you didn't know enough about it to be dangerous. I kept it that way for this very reason.
In the midst of that debacle, we at least managed to retrieve the kill-code. The usual brain-trust has come up with an alternate plan on how to use it, based around a recent finding. Malphas will give you as many of the details as you need to know.
As far as I'm concerned, this is all just going to show that trying to kill someone who can see it coming is a waste of time. But nobody ever listens to me...

enter.say: The "brain trust" appears to be holding court.

talk.say:
A key has been unearthed at the Mahath Tower construction site in Lamar. The key was made by the Keymaker; Mahath is the former site of the government building where he was killed by Agent Smith, after Zionites abducted him from the Merovingian's safe-keeping. The key was on his keychain at the time, and was buried when the building was destroyed just after his death. It was to be used to aid in killing the Oracle. As it turned out, it was not needed. Now, however, it once again has a use.
The key will be given to our new Oracle assassin, along with the kill-code. The Merovingian is about to negotiate for the transportation of this assassin.

done.say: He'd better not be made out of flies.

talk.say:
It is the General who will be supplying our new assassin. He should be contacting us from the outside world by a special broadcast channel I've arranged...
Ah, here he comes now.
Welcome, monsieur! We need a squad of your best men for the Oracle project. Surely you can spare a few, non?

done.say: Oh, heck. I was hoping we'd seen the last of that guy. You'd better see what's gonna happen with this.

talk.say:
...
If it is for the purpose of killing the Oracle, then...very well. I will need them back in one piece.
I understand that the Machines got to the Trainman. Someone will have to configure and run the transfer program on alternate hardware.

done.say: Ooh, he's got a point there. How are we going to transport programs into the Matrix without the Trainman?

phase.briefing:
Oh, typical. "We've lost an employee, so let's just give his work to that incredibly competent Flood." That's the danger of being too good at your job--not that you have to worry about that.
As usual, it's up to me to put things right...
Fine. First, you're going to get the General's troop transfer program from the Trainman's workshop.

enter.say:
Were you ever tempted just to abort the mission, and tell the Merv it was Flood's fault?
Right, right... Anyway, that's the Trainman's place. Got some computer systems and Exile programs inside.

done.say:
Not seeing a lot of friendly faces in there... No wonder the Trainman was always cranky.
Wait a sec... According to that readout, someone just pulled data off that machine. They're trying to pull a fast one on us! One of them must have the transfer program.
Sheesh... Okay, get on out of there.

phase.briefing: The Effectuator will be executing the transfer program, {player}. He's supposed to be capable of handling such things... I suppose it will be my good deed of the day if I manage to expose him for the bubble-headed fraud he really is.

done.say: So is he gonna make the magic happen, or what?

objective.text: Give the Data to the Effectuator

done.say:
Hey! Spiffy program! All right, let's crank this baby up...
Here she goes!
... Oops.
Umm...kay. We may need to talk to Flood about this.

complete.say:
Ohh, you need to give the thing bit parameters, and a receiving matrix...
Hey, how was I supposed to know? It's an unintuitive interface!
Look, don't worry about a thing. I can make this work. I just...er...have to go look something up.

phase.briefing:
I've had a little chat with the Effectuator, {player}. He assures me that he has worked out "the kinks" in the process. I have my doubts.
You'll need to run a command from a specific computer at the marked location in order to initiate what had better be a successful transfer...

enter.say: That's the place. Let's hope this works.

done.say: Looks clear. You'd better hurry up with that transfer, though.
They made it? Thank goodness. I'd get out of there before the Effectuator shows up to gloat.

near.say:
There's the computer. Now just--
Uh-oh. I've got Machines on the screen! Heads up!
You are in violation of System protocols concerning the download of illegal programs.
You are in violation of System protocols concerning the download of illegal programs.

mission.finish:
Four programs transferred intact, one crippled, three terminated: I suppose that counts as a blinding success in the Effectuator's books.
Not that I'm about to cry over spilt commandos; there are always more where those came from. Whether or not one of them armed with the key and the code can actually kill the Oracle is another question.
